A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same abstraction-learning framework. Their text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable matching across renaming and relocation. Minor delimiter-rendering defects in v3 do not prevent comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSM-Symbolic and GSM-Plus experiments across multiple LLMs, component ablations, and qualitative examples in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluated baselines and zero-shot mathematical and general-reasoning results in Tables 3, 6, and 7.

M1.justification: The four-stage framework, GranulAR construction, supervised training, and GRPO with answer-correctness and symbolic-distance rewards remain unchanged. AbstraL becomes AbstRaL, but the additional evaluations do not establish a changed algorithm or inference procedure.

E1.justification: v3 expands evaluation beyond GSM8K-derived perturbations to eleven additional mathematical benchmarks, including MATH, AIME24, TABMWP, and College-Math, plus MMLU, BBH, ARC-Challenge, and OpenBookQA. Section 5.2 and Tables 6–7 document substantially broader task coverage. GSM training data and existing perturbation coverage remain unchanged.

E2.justification: v3 Table 1 adds PoT-8S, AoT, and SyReLM to the GSM comparisons for Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct. The transfer experiments also introduce the original checkpoints as Ori-SFT comparators alongside CoT-RL and CoA. The original comparator membership remains intact in the retained appendix comparisons.

E3.justification: Section 5.2 adds a zero-shot transfer evaluation of two Qwen models and their original checkpoints. This is a new evaluation setting, not a revision of the retained GSM experiments: template sampling, test sizes, training budgets, model configurations, and greedy decoding remain unchanged. Detailed OOD prompting and scoring procedures are not supplied.

E4.justification: The new transfer study explicitly tests whether GSM-focused training benefits other reasoning tasks or overfits GSM, adding an analysis beyond the original within-GSM perturbation tests. Existing component ablations and both qualitative cases are retained. v1's brief pilot reports about direct X-to-A abstraction and alternative CoA hyperparameters are omitted.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations across 50 GSM-Symbolic template-resampling rounds and bootstrap comparisons using p < 0.05. No new seed information, run-count policy, or statistical procedure is introduced. The added OOD tables report point estimates without additional uncertainty analysis.

E6.justification: v3 adds results for three GSM baselines and the OOD evaluations. For example, Table 7 newly reports Qwen2.5-Math-7B-Instruct BBH scores of 54.8 for AbstRaL, 43.7 for Ori-SFT, 46.0 for CoT-RL, and 42.9 for CoA. These have no v1 counterpart. Retained GSM and tabulated ablation values match after accounting for percentage conversion and rounding.

T1.justification: The abstraction assumptions and reward, GRPO, KL, and advantage equations remain substantively unchanged. v1's theoretical open problems move to Appendix F. The new Section 5.3 offers conceptual explanations and explicitly leaves formalization to future work; it adds no theorem, proof, or formal derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion add a central claim that learning abstraction on GSM implicitly improves zero-shot mathematical and general reasoning beyond GSM. v1 claims robustness on GSM perturbations without this transfer contribution. v3 also makes the framework's direct GSM focus more explicit while retaining the granular abstraction and RL contributions.

C2.justification: Sections 5.2–5.3 interpret transfer as an implicit benefit of abstract thinking and add explanations involving fluid intelligence, globality, and reduced shortcut learning. Appendix G clarifies that the restricted domain coverage concerns robustness testing. Most original interpretations and limitations remain, although the caveat attributing residual numerical-shift errors to condition recognition is omitted.

D1.justification: The proposed method's hyperparameters, hardware, processing times, filtering counts, and three prompt tables are preserved and consolidated in Appendix B. However, v1's CoA implementation appendix and prompt table disappear, including its oracle/data matching and SFT-setting disclosures. This reduces baseline reproducibility information without establishing an actual change to CoA training.

R1.justification: v3 substantially expands positioning around program and formal-language reasoning through PoT, PAL, and SyReLM, alongside citations for the added benchmarks. Appendix C acknowledges that SyReLM already uses RL and symbolic rewards, shifting the distinction toward integration with natural-language reasoning rather than comparison only with SFT-based abstraction methods. The tree-of-thought reference is removed.

P1.justification: The experimental-settings section is compressed, implementation and baseline material is consolidated in Appendices B–C, and results are organized into robustness, transfer, and discussion subsections. Theoretical open problems and limitations move to Appendices F–G, and references precede the appendices. The title and method capitalization also change.

P2.justification: v3 merges the main GSM comparisons into one table, condenses displayed columns, and adds OOD summary and full-result tables. It removes the CoA prompt table, revises diagram labels, and adopts a different conference layout. Some appendix angle-bracket delimiters are visibly misrendered as inverted punctuation, introducing a presentation defect.

improvement.justification: v3 strengthens assessment of the central method through more relevant comparators, especially RL-based SyReLM, and adds evidence addressing v1's untested transfer beyond GSM. Its research positioning is also more complete. These benefits are partly offset by missing OOD prompting/scoring details, removal of CoA reproducibility information, and corrupted appendix delimiters. The resulting net improvement is meaningful but limited.
